blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Neolithic Age marked the transition from a nomadic hunting-gathering lifestyle to settled agriculture and food production.
Earliest agricultural evidence in the Indian subcontinent for wheat and barley cultivation comes from Mehrgarh in Balochistan.
Neolithic tools were characterized by polished, ground stone equipment, including stone axes, adzes, and polished celts.
Invention of the potter's wheel enabled the production of distinct pottery types like grey ware, black burnished ware, and cord-impressed pottery.
Unique settlement practices emerged, such as pit-dwellings and burying domestic dogs with their owners at Burzahom in Kashmir.

blocks.content: The Neolithic Age generally extended from 6,000 BC to 1,000 BC, though the exact time varies from region to region.

The Neolithic Age marked a major transformation in human life, often referred to as the Neolithic Revolution. During this period: - Humans began agriculture. - Animals were domesticated. - People started living in permanent settlements.
The Neolithic Revolution transformed human culture from food gatherers into food producers, laying the foundation for permanent human settlements.
SSC Highlight: Agriculture began in the Neolithic Age.

items: Tools were made of polished stone, making them sharper and more durable.
These tools were mainly used for farming and clearing forests.
Houses were made of mud and bricks.
Grains were stored for future use.

blocks.content: Commonly domesticated animals included: - Cow - Goat - Sheep - Dog

items: Burzahom (Kashmir) is frequently tested for its unique pit-dwellings and domestic dog burials alongside human graves.
Chirand (Bihar) is famous for its remarkable concentration of tools made of bone and stag antlers.
Mehrgarh is the key site for early cotton cultivation and rectangular mud-brick structures in South Asia.
Daojali Hading (Assam) is prominent for cord-impressed pottery and imported jadeite tools.
Humans started wearing clothes made from cotton and wool.
